summary: Turnbull NWR, Spokane County: a 1938 fire tower of 99 ft with an L-6 cab, in ruins by 1971; WillhiteWeb says hiking to the site is restricted.

access.note: WillhiteWeb says the refuge prohibits hiking in this area except in hunting season, for hunters with special permits; signs at the gate say no entry.

visit.trail_note: Hiking here is prohibited except in hunting season for special-permit hunters. Do not visit without refuge permission.

facts.status_note: Tower in ruins by 1971; footings and timbers appear in WillhiteWeb's photos. Hiking to the site is prohibited on this refuge land except in hunting season.

events.note: USGS benchmark placed at the site; the survey described the tower as 108.8 feet tall. A refuge photo dated September 5, 1952 is captioned as a view from the fire tower
Ruins on the ground by 1971; the sources do not say how the tower came down
Registered December 17, 2012 (US 1532, WA 432), nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 99 feet for the 1938 tower. WillhiteWeb also reports a 1952 USGS description of 108.8 feet. The story uses 99 feet and flags the difference for checking against the USGS record.

sources.title: Low water levels at Lower Turnbull Lake
sources.publisher: Turnbull National Wildlife Refuge Photographs, Eastern Washington University Digital Commons

notes_for_editor: Build year, L-6 cab and 1971 ruins agree across three pages. Height disagrees (99 ft versus a 1952 USGS 108.8 ft quoted by WillhiteWeb). The tower's fate and the date of its removal or collapse are not documented. Site access and the footings come from WillhiteWeb's undated text and captions. The EWU archive holds the refuge's 1939-40 narrative reports, which may record construction; they were not read. One web search gave no further tower detail.
